subject: Possible to get more than 3 decimal places in output?

messages.author: 39ba3d2da294963f
messages.subject: Possible to get more than 3 decimal places in output?
parts: Hello, I was wondering if there is a way to obtain non-rounded values from a fitted lavaan object?  For instance, inspect(fit, "rsquare") only provides 3 decimal places, as do many other output functions.  I need greater precision for my application.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Possible to get more than 3 decimal places in output?
parts: Hello, I was wondering if there is a way to obtain non-rounded values from a fitted lavaan object?

Yves includes an argument "nd" in his print methods for lavaan vectors/matrices/data.frames (with nd = 3 as the default setting).  So you can either use the print function:

> print(inspect(fit, "rsquare"), nd = 5)
     x1      x2      x3      x4      x5      x6      x7      x8      x9 
0.59580 0.17944 0.33771 0.72519 0.73114 0.70226 0.32435 0.52279 0.44224 


Or you can just strip the "lavaan.vector" class so that it is printed like a regular numeric vector:

> unclass(inspect(fit, "rsquare"))
       x1        x2        x3        x4        x5        x6        x7        x8        x9 
0.5957994 0.1794378 0.3377148 0.7251923 0.7311369 0.7022609 0.3243470 0.5227933 0.4422373 


Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Possible to get more than 3 decimal places in output?
parts:
Another trick (since 0.5-17) is to use the function lavTech() instead of
inspect(). They are identical, but lavTech() does (per default) not
prettify the output.

> example(cfa)
> lavTech(fit, "rsquare")
[[1]]
[1] 0.5957994 0.1794378 0.3377148 0.7251923 0.7311369 0.7022609 0.3243470
[8] 0.5227933 0.4422373


or if you do not want to be wrapped in a list:

lavTech(fit, "rsquare", drop.list.single.group = TRUE)


Yves.
